changes.balance: The premium is repriced, not removed: the price recovered for two sessions on an unchanged physical board, with strait transit still below 60 percent of capacity on the ANZ gauge and tanker attacks at a record pace, while the balance gauges point the other way, with J.P. Morgan holding a 1.4 million barrel a day global surplus in October. The congressional constraint behind Wednesday's repricing binds only from Jan 3, and the desks still price renewed strikes at 60 percent.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled at $98.29 on Thursday, up $3.67 or 3.9 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $90.52, up $2.40 or 2.7 percent (Bloomberg via Rigzone), recovering part of Wednesday's $8.98 and $7.97 falls. Overnight Brent briefly traded above $100 before holding at $99.58, up $1.29, with WTI at $91.38, up 86 cents, at 0504 GMT (Reuters, Nov 6). Both benchmarks remain down about 12 percent on the week. Talks remain far apart on Tehran's own account, and UKMTO counts at least five vessel incidents since Sunday, close to October's record pace of 35 vessels hit; Iranian mine claims for Thursday are unconfirmed and are not summed with the UKMTO count. December WCS is -$30.15 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 5) on zero lots, and December Houston is -$20.27 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 5), putting the export spread at +$9.88. The validated diesel crack is $91.94.
changes.conditional: A settle back above $100 with the incident pace continuing grades Wednesday as a flush inside an intact premium structure; a fade back toward $94 grades the reset as holding. A published acceptance in the mediator process would start the reopening sequence the lower level is discounting.
changes.delta: Thursday settles: Brent Jan27 $98.29, up $3.67 or 3.9 percent; WTI Dec26 $90.52, up $2.40 or 2.7 percent (Bloomberg via Rigzone). Overnight Brent $99.58 and WTI $91.38 at 0504 GMT, Brent briefly above $100 (Reuters). Both benchmarks down about 12 percent on the week. UKMTO: at least five vessel incidents since Sunday, against 35 in October. December WCS -$30.15 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 5) on zero lots. December Houston -$20.27 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 5), spread +$9.88. Diesel crack $91.94 on the validated history.
changes.source: Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 5, 2026; Reuters, Nov 5-6, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 5, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 6, 2026
changes.title: Brent recovered a second day and briefly traded above $100, grading Wednesday as a premium level reset with the escalation branch still live

changes.balance: The strip is paying for the spring exit and not for December. December has printed wide on traded volume in four of the last six sessions and has not yet tightened on volume, so the front remains a space and freight price while the deferred tenors price the episode's end.
changes.body: December WCS is -$30.15 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 5) on zero lots, so the tightening is a mark, not a traded settle, and carries no verdict until December trades. The strip behind it tightened on real volume for a second straight session: Jan27 -$25.00 on 2 lots, Feb27 -$24.35 on 1 lot, Mar27 -$22.70 on 1 lot, Apr27 -$20.40 on 835 lots, May27 -$18.60 on 835 lots and Jun27 -$16.95 on 835 lots, with Jul27 through Sep27 each on 475 lots. The recovery slope from December to June is about $2.20 a month. December Houston is -$20.27 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 5) on zero lots, and the December export spread held at +$9.88 because both legs marked tighter together.
changes.conditional: A December settle tighter on traded volume would be the first traded confirmation that the front is healing; another wide traded December print, or a December apportionment notice at or above November levels, extends the episode.
changes.delta: December WCS -$30.15 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 5), marked $0.94 tighter on zero lots. Apr27 -$20.40, May27 -$18.60 and Jun27 -$16.95, each on 835 lots; Jul27 to Sep27 each on 475 lots. December Houston -$20.27 on zero lots; December ARV to TMW spread +$9.88, January +$7.25. December last traded wide at -$31.08 on Nov 4 (120 lots).
changes.title: December WCS tightened only as a zero-lot mark while the deferred strip tightened on traded volume for a second straight session

changes.balance: With Horizon confirmed, every major fall maintenance item is operator-confirmed complete, so no maintenance leg supports the wide front. What holds December wide is November apportionment and freight against record supply, and the Keystone restriction lift is egress returning in phases rather than leaving.
changes.body: Canadian Natural Resources released third quarter results on Nov 5: production of about 1,652,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day, net earnings of about C$3.0 billion and adjusted funds flow of about C$5.5 billion. The Horizon turnaround completed after quarter-end in 28 days, seven days ahead of schedule, which closes the last unconfirmed major fall maintenance item, and three-year intervals between Horizon turnarounds are now planned instead of two-year intervals. Thermal in-situ production was a record 300,000 barrels a day. South Bow reported Keystone throughput of about 586 kb/d in the third quarter, said the Milepost 171 pressure restrictions are being lifted in phases on certain segments through the end of 2026 into 2027, and closed its Prairie Connector open season with nine customers making binding 20-year commitments for 465 kb/d toward a targeted mid-2027 investment decision.
changes.conditional: Enbridge reporting today, with Mainline volumes and any December colour, is the remaining egress print before nominations close Nov 17. A December apportionment notice is the next dated egress event.
changes.delta: Canadian Natural (Nov 5): Horizon turnaround completed after quarter-end in 28 days against a planned 35; production about 1,652,000 BOE/d; thermal in-situ a record 300,000 bbl/d; net debt C$12.117 billion, below the C$13 billion target. South Bow (Nov 4-5): Keystone Q3 throughput about 586 kb/d; Milepost 171 pressure restrictions lifting in phases through end-2026 into 2027; Prairie Connector commitments 465 kb/d from nine customers on binding 20-year terms.
changes.source: Canadian Natural Resources third quarter 2026 results, Nov 5, 2026; South Bow third quarter 2026 results, Nov 4, 2026, and call, Nov 5, 2026
changes.title: Horizon is confirmed complete seven days early, closing the fall maintenance season, and Keystone pressure restrictions are lifting in phases

flags.body: Brent settled at $98.29 on Thursday after Wednesday's $8.98 fall, recovering on a physical board that did not change: talks far apart, the Supreme Leader ruling out any inclination towards submission, and UKMTO incidents running at October's record pace, with Iranian mine claims for Thursday unconfirmed. Eurasia Group prices renewed strikes at 60 percent with a $110 to $125 Brent band, a deal at 10 percent and a standoff at 30 percent. The new Congress is seated Jan 3, 2027; until then the administration's foreign policy runs under the existing composition.
flags.title: The war premium repriced on politics: no deal, no accepted terms, and the escalation branch still priced at 60 percent
flags.trigger: A published agreement or acceptance in the mediator process, a confirmed strike or maritime escalation, a settle confirming or reversing the recovery, or the Abu Dhabi talks on Nov 10-11

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack now includes five wide traded December settlements (-$31.10 on Oct 28, -$30.69 on Nov 2, -$31.25 on Nov 3, -$31.08 on Nov 4, with Nov 5 marked tighter on zero lots) and a deferred strip that tightened on 835-lot volume in April through June for two straight sessions, pricing the episode's exit. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record.
flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop

flags.body: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003 and 13 percent below the five-year average, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. PADD 2 distillate drew 1.4 million to 22.8 million in the same week. The validated diesel crack is $91.94, up from $88.73, and total commercial petroleum inventories fell 8.2 million barrels on the week. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12.
flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003: the products leg is the tight part of the US balance into winter
flags.trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction
